title: Chapter 3 Quiz 16
description: Traps in every question. Read the code line by line and do not trust the first impression.
topic: Difficult: loops, recursion and hidden errors
instructions: Chapter 3: Difficult: loops, recursion and hidden errors.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: This recursive function should return N!. One line breaks it. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Function Fact(N) Returns integer
Begin
    If N = 0 Then
        Fact ← 1
    Else
        Fact ← N * Fact(N + 1)
    EndIf
End Function
questions.explanation: The call must use a smaller value to reach the base case N = 0. With N + 1 the values grow and the function never stops.

questions.question: This should display the smallest of the 5 values in tab. Two lines have an error.
questions.code:
Let min ← 0
For i From 1 To 5 Do
    If tab[i] > min Then
        min ← tab[i]
    EndIf
EndDo
Display(min)
questions.explanation: Line 1: min must start with the first element, tab[1] (0 could be smaller than every value). Line 3: we replace min when the new value is smaller, so the test is tab[i] < min.

questions.question:
How many times does the body run?
```
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From i To 4 Do
        Display(i, j)
    EndDo
EndDo
```
questions.explanation: i = 1 gives 4 passes, i = 2 gives 3, i = 3 gives 2 and i = 4 gives 1. The total is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.
questions.hint: The inner loop starts at i, not at 1.

questions.question:
How many numbers does this algorithm display?
```
Let i ← 10
Repeat
    Display(i)
    i ← i + 1
Until i > 5
```
questions.explanation: Repeat...Until tests after the body, so 10 is displayed once. Then i = 11 and 11 > 5 is true, so the loop stops.

questions.question: Trace this loop: i ← 20, then While i > 3 Do i ← i - 6. Fill in the table.
questions.explanation: 20 → 14 → 8 → 2. After the third pass i = 2, so 2 > 3 is False and the loop ends after 3 passes.

questions.question: This selection sort swaps tab[i] and tab[minIndex]. One line of the swap is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
temp ← tab[i]
tab[i] ← tab[minIndex]
tab[minIndex] ← tab[i]
questions.explanation: After line 2, tab[i] already holds the new value, so the old value of tab[i] would be lost. The saved old value is in temp.

questions.question: The recursive Fibonacci F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2), with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1, is written without memoization. How many calls of F are made in total to compute F(5), counting the first call?
questions.explanation: Calls: c(0) = c(1) = 1, and c(n) = 1 + c(n-1) + c(n-2). That gives 1, 1, 3, 5, 9, 15. This is why memoization matters.
questions.hint: Count calls, not the value of F.

questions.question: Which of these statements are **true**?
options: A While loop tests its condition after the first pass
For i From 5 To 1 does not run when the step is +1
A Repeat loop whose Until test is true at the start still runs once
A While loop whose test is false at the start runs 0 times
For i From 1 To 0 runs the body one time
questions.explanation: While tests first (0 times is possible). A For loop with the start above the end does not run. Repeat...Until always runs once before testing. For i From 1 To 0 is an empty range, and While never tests after the body.

questions.question: Evaluate each expression (the brackets show the order).
questions.explanation: 17 MOD 5 = 2 and 17 DIV 5 = 3; 20 DIV 3 = 6 and 20 MOD 3 = 2.

questions.question: This should display the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5. One line makes the loop run for ever. Find it.
questions.code:
Let i ← 1
Let total ← 0
While i <= 5 Do
    total ← total + i
    i ← i - 1
EndDo
Display(total)
questions.explanation: i must go up so that i <= 5 eventually becomes false. With i ← i - 1 the test is true for ever.

questions.assertion: In For i From 1 To N, when N = 0 the body runs once.
questions.reason: The initial and final values of a For loop are both included.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false: the range 1 to 0 is empty, so the body does not run. The reason is true, but it does not make the assertion hold.
